title: A New Route Through the Botanic Grounds
transcript:
Welcome to the botanic grounds. Today's walk uses a new route through the northern section, which reopened last month. Some of you may remember a path that went straight across the lawn. That shortcut is now closed so the soil can recover, and the new route follows the edge of the planted areas instead.

We begin at the glasshouse. Please leave any large umbrellas in the stand outside, since the aisles are narrow. The collection inside includes plants adapted to long dry periods. Look at the different ways they reduce water loss; not all of them have the thick stems that visitors usually associate with dry climates.

When we come outside, we will stop beside the orchard. The young trees have labels giving the variety and the year they were planted. The fruit is used for teaching and research, so visitors should not pick it, even when it has fallen onto the path. Staff collect fallen fruit to check for signs of disease.

Further along, a small shelter contains a map showing changes to the grounds over two centuries. The lake appears much larger on the oldest drawing. It gradually became shallower as soil washed in from nearby fields, and its present outline was created during repairs in the previous century.

The route then crosses an area of meadow. We cut this at different times of year, leaving some strips standing while others are mown. The uneven appearance is intentional. It gives insects somewhere to move when a neighbouring strip is cut and allows staff to compare which plants return.

If you would prefer a shorter walk, a level path from the shelter leads directly back to the entrance. It avoids the meadow slope and takes about ten minutes at an easy pace. A volunteer will accompany anyone who chooses that option, so there is no need to leave the group alone.

At the end of the visit, the education team will demonstrate how to collect seeds without damaging the parent plant. You can practise with material prepared by the gardeners. Please do not gather samples elsewhere in the grounds; some collections contain rare varieties that look very ordinary.

Finally, our photographs policy allows pictures for personal use. If you include other visitors, ask their permission first. Tripods are permitted outdoors when they do not block a path, but they must remain folded inside the glasshouse because space there is limited.

questions.prompt: Visitors must not collect fruit from the ____.
questions.explanation: 果园的果实用于教学研究，落果也不应取走。

questions.prompt: A historical map can be found in a small ____.
questions.explanation: 小凉亭内展示两个世纪的园区变化地图。

questions.prompt: Why are different meadow strips cut at different times?
options: To leave refuge for insects and compare plant growth
To prepare the whole area for new buildings
To keep all plants at the same height
questions.answer: To leave refuge for insects and compare plant growth
questions.explanation: 分区错时修剪给昆虫留庇护处，并利于比较植物恢复。

questions.prompt: Where are tripods not allowed to be opened?
questions.explanation: 温室通道狭窄，三脚架必须折叠。
